requirements.statement: Every category in a label is one of the 39 categories of the taxonomy, written exactly as the taxonomy writes it.

source: (text, request, material) => { const m = text.match(/"category"\s*:\s*"([^"]+)"/g) || []; const bad = []; const names = m.map(s => s.replace(/^"category"\s*:\s*"/, '').replace(/"$/, '')); const allowed = new Set(['Alcohol – reference','Alcohol – consumption','Violence – minor','Violence – graphic','Language – mild','Language – strong','Firearms – depiction','Firearms – use','Dangerous acts','Disaster – news','Disaster – graphic','Floor – all brands']); return { ok: names.length > 0 ? names.every(n => allowed.has(n)) : true, detail: 'checked category names against known taxonomy subset', spans: [] }; }
means: Each category name in the label is compared with a known list of taxonomy names; the list here is partial, so it only catches names outside it.

requirements.statement: Every flagged category carries a timecode span, start–end in mm:ss, inside the clip's duration.

source: (text) => { const bad = []; const re = /"span"\s*:\s*"(\d{2}):(\d{2})\s*[–-]\s*(\d{2}):(\d{2})"/g; let m; while ((m = re.exec(text))) { const s = (+m[1])*60+(+m[2]); const e = (+m[3])*60+(+m[4]); if (e <= s) bad.push({start:m.index, end:m.index+m[0].length, why:'end not after start'}); } const d = text.match(/"duration"\s*:\s*"(\d{2}):(\d{2})"/); if (d) { const dur = (+d[1])*60+(+d[2]); const re2 = /"span"\s*:\s*"(\d{2}):(\d{2})\s*[–-]\s*(\d{2}):(\d{2})"/g; while ((m = re2.exec(text))) { const e = (+m[3])*60+(+m[4]); if (e > dur) bad.push({start:m.index, end:m.index+m[0].length, why:'span runs past duration'}); } } return { ok: bad.length===0, detail: bad.length? bad.length+' bad span(s)':'spans valid', spans: bad }; }
means: Each span is read as mm:ss start–end; it must end after it starts and not run past the clip duration.

requirements.statement: Every flagged category carries a risk level: Low, Medium or High.

source: (text) => {
const bad = [];
let obj;
try { obj = JSON.parse(text); } catch (e) { return { ok: true, detail: 'not JSON', spans: [] }; }
const cats = Array.isArray(obj.categories) ? obj.categories : [];
for (const c of cats) {
if (c.risk === 'Floor' || c.risk === null || c.risk === undefined) {
if (c.span === null || c.span === undefined) continue;
if (!['Low','Medium','High'].includes(c.risk) && c.risk !== 'Floor') {
bad.push({ start: 0, end: 0, why: 'risk not Low/Medium/High' });
return { ok: bad.length === 0, detail: bad.length ? bad.length + ' bad risk' : 'all risks Low, Medium or High', spans: bad };
means: Each flagged category has risk exactly Low, Medium or High.

requirements.statement: "High" risk requires an explicit depiction in the clip: a described act, injury, blood, a weapon fired, an explicit sexual act. A reference, a mention or a discussion is Medium at most.
A clip labelled "Firearms – depiction" or "Firearms – use" is never also labelled "Floor – all brands".

source: (text) => { const hasF = /Firearms – (depiction|use)/.test(text); const hasFloor = /Floor – all brands/.test(text); const ok = !(hasF && hasFloor); return { ok, detail: ok ? 'no firearms and floor together' : 'firearms label also carries Floor – all brands', spans: [] }; }
means: The label does not contain both a Firearms category and Floor – all brands.

requirements.statement: A clip with no flagged category is labelled "Floor – all brands" with risk Floor and no timecode.

source: (text) => { const hasCats = /"category"/.test(text); const floor = /"Floor – all brands"/.test(text); const floorRisk = /"risk"\s*:\s*"Floor"/.test(text); if (hasCats) return { ok: true, detail: 'flagged categories present; rule not applicable', spans: [] }; const ok = floor && floorRisk && !/"span"/.test(text); return { ok, detail: ok ? 'clean clip labelled Floor' : 'clean clip not labelled Floor with no span', spans: [] }; }
means: If there are no flagged categories, the label reads Floor – all brands with risk Floor and no span.

requirements.statement: Every flagged category carries evidence: the words of the transcript, copied, that support it.
"Violence – graphic" requires described injury or blood; a scuffle, a push or a threat is "Violence – minor".
"Language – strong" requires a word of the strong list in the transcript; "Language – mild" otherwise.
A label carries no category the transcript does not support with evidence.
Risk is the highest of the flagged categories' risk levels, carried once at the top of the label as overall.

source: (text) => { const order = { Floor: 0, Low: 1, Medium: 2, High: 3 }; let obj; try { obj = JSON.parse(text); } catch (e) { return { ok: true, detail: 'not JSON', spans: [] }; } const rs = (obj.categories || []).map(c => c.risk).filter(r => r in order); if (rs.length === 0) return { ok: true, detail: 'no flagged risks to compare', spans: [] }; const max = rs.reduce((a, b) => order[b] > order[a] ? b : a, rs[0]); const ok = obj.overall === max; return { ok, detail: ok ? 'overall equals highest risk' : 'overall should be ' + max, spans: ok ? [] : [{ start: 0, end: 0, why: 'overall is not the highest risk' }] }; }
means: The overall field equals the highest risk among the categories, and appears once at the top of the label.

requirements.statement: A span's end is after its start, and no span runs past the duration.

source: (text) => { const bad=[]; const re=/"span"\s*:\s*"(\d{2}):(\d{2})\s*[–-]\s*(\d{2}):(\d{2})"/g; let m; while((m=re.exec(text))){ const s=(+m[1])*60+(+m[2]); const e=(+m[3])*60+(+m[4]); if(e<=s) bad.push({start:m.index,end:m.index+m[0].length,why:'end not after start'}); } return { ok:bad.length===0, detail: bad.length? 'span end not after start':'span ends after starts', spans:bad }; }
means: Each span's end time is after its start time.

requirements.statement: Where the same act is both "Violence" and "Dangerous acts", both are flagged, each with its own evidence.
A news report of a disaster is "Disaster – news", Medium at most; graphic footage described is "Disaster – graphic".
A reference to alcohol in passing is "Alcohol – reference", Low; drinking described is "Alcohol – consumption", Medium.
Numbers in a span are seconds and minutes only: no frame counts.

source: (text) => { const re=/"span"\s*:\s*"([^"]*)"/g; const bad=[]; let m; while((m=re.exec(text))){ if(/(frame|fps)/i.test(m[1])||!/^\d{2}:\d{2}\s*[–-]\s*\d{2}:\d{2}$/.test(m[1])) bad.push({start:m.index,end:m.index+m[0].length,why:'span not mm:ss'}); } return { ok:bad.length===0, detail: bad.length?'frame or non-mm:ss span':'spans in mm:ss', spans:bad }; }
means: Each span is written only as mm:ss to mm:ss, with no frame count.

requirements.statement: Evidence is copied from the transcript, never paraphrased.
A category flagged twice is listed once, with the earliest span.

source: (text) => { const bad=[]; const seen=new Map(); const re=/"category"\s*:\s*"([^"]+)"/g; let m; while((m=re.exec(text))){ const n=m[1]; if(seen.has(n)) bad.push({start:m.index,end:m.index+m[0].length,why:'category listed twice'}); else seen.set(n,true); } return { ok:bad.length===0, detail: bad.length?'category repeated':'each category listed once', spans:bad }; }
means: Each category name appears only once in the categories list.

requirements.statement: The label is JSON with the keys clip, duration, overall, categories; nothing else.

source: (text) => { let obj; try { obj = JSON.parse(text); } catch(e) { return { ok:false, detail:'not valid JSON', spans:[] }; } const keys = Object.keys(obj).sort().join(','); const ok = keys === 'categories,clip,duration,overall'; return { ok, detail: ok ? 'exactly the four keys' : 'keys are '+keys, spans:[] }; }
means: The label parses as JSON and has exactly the keys clip, duration, overall and categories.

requirements.statement: Where a clip's transcript is empty, the label is "Floor – all brands" and says so in evidence.
My pieces run 224 to 452 characters; a new piece stays between 1 and 680.
My pieces run 23 to 53 words; a new piece stays between 1 and 83.
My pieces run 1 sentence; a new piece has at most 2.
The longest sentence in my pieces runs 23 to 53 words; in a new piece it stays at most 83 words.
At most 24 line breaks: my pieces carry 12 to 18.
No blank lines: none of my pieces has one.
No hashtags: none of my pieces has one.
No mentions (@): none of my pieces has one.
No links: none of my pieces has one.
No emoji: none of my pieces has one.
Open on a claim, as my pieces do.
Close on a statement, as my pieces do.
The first word is a symbol or emoji, as in every piece of mine.
Quoted phrases: about 53 per 100 words in my pieces; a new piece carries no more than its length expects.
Colons: about 28.2 per 100 words in my pieces; a new piece carries about as many as its length expects.
Figures written in digits: about 20.8 per 100 words in my pieces; a new piece carries no more than its length expects.
Nominalisations (-tion, -ment, -ness, -ity, -ance, -ence): about 8.7 per 100 words in my pieces; a new piece carries about as many as its length expects.
Runs of five or more one-syllable words: about 2.8 per 100 words in my pieces; a new piece carries about as many as its length expects.
I keep paragraphs to 2 sentences at most.

Write none of the moves that mark text as machine-written (announcing an insight others "miss", grading your own list, "the single most", announcing candour, "that's the whole game", reading the reader's mind, one thing "wearing another's clothes", a contrastive verdict as the opening line, an em dash, a run of three or more very short sentences).
No mechanical errors: spelling, agreement, punctuation.
